purpose: Public identifiers from the project's verified experiments. These are reproducibility inputs, not secret configuration.

routes.name: External Arbitrum -> HyperCore
routes.matchingRule: The Arbitrum transaction hash is repeated as the HyperCore deposit hash; also verify user, asset and amount.
routes.limitation: This exact-hash rule was verified for the native Arbitrum deposit route and must not be generalized to every bridge.

routes.name: HyperCore -> External Arbitrum
routes.matchingRule: Join destination, asset, ledger fee, net received amount and time; the Core and Arbitrum hashes differ.
routes.limitation: Withdrawal fees can change and must be read from the observed ledger update rather than hard-coded.

routes.name: HyperCore wallet -> HyperCore wallet
routes.matchingRule: Read the Core send action and verify user, destination, token and amount.
routes.limitation: There is no EVM transaction; historical balance deltas require saved snapshots or archival state.

routes.name: HyperCore -> same-address HyperEVM
routes.matchingRule: Join user, HYPE, exact amount and close time between the Core send and custom-RPC System TX.
routes.limitation: Hashes differ, and standard EVM transaction/receipt calls may return null for the System TX.

routes.name: HyperEVM -> same-address HyperCore
routes.matchingRule: Join sender/user, HYPE, exact amount and close time between the user EVM transfer to the system address and Core credit.
routes.limitation: Hashes differ; repeated identical transfers in the same window can create multiple candidates.

routes.name: HyperEVM wallet -> HyperEVM wallet
routes.matchingRule: Retrieve the exact transaction hash and verify successful receipt plus from, to and value.
routes.limitation: The transaction proves transfer, not common control of the two wallets.

routes.name: External Bitcoin -> HyperEVM
routes.matchingRule: The exact 32-byte protocol identifier occurs in both Bitcoin OP_RETURN and the HyperEVM destination transaction input.
routes.limitation: The identifier location is bridge-specific; other bridges require their own event/status decoder.

routes.name: HyperEVM -> Base through LI.FI
routes.matchingRule: Official LI.FI status binds exact sending and receiving hashes under one transactionId.
routes.limitation: If the status record expires or is unavailable, protocol-event decoding is required.

routes.name: HyperEVM -> Ethereum through LI.FI
routes.matchingRule: Official LI.FI status binds exact sending and receiving hashes under one transactionId even when asset and recipient change.
routes.limitation: Do not require equal amounts, assets or addresses across a bridge/swap route.
